The petitioner is the accused in Crime No.826/2025 of Chavakkad Police Station.

The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Section 376 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Section 64 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Sections 4(2) read with Section 3(a), 3(b), 6 read with Section 5(l), 5(m), 8 read with Section 7, 10 read with Section 9(l), 9(m), 12 read with Section 11(vi) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.

sentences.text:
3. The prosecution case as narrated in Anx.A2 order reads thus:
"At the time when the survivor girl was studying in 5th standard, while she was going to the shop of the accused at Munakkakadavu for purchase, the accused sexually assaulted her by catching hold on her cheeks and private parts by 2025:KER:94344 offering chocolates and lays.

On another day, he took her inside the shop, disrobed her and inserted her finger into her vagina and later by inserting his penis into her anus and on 21.09.2025 also he again committed grave penetrative sexual assault on her."(sic)
4. The petitioner was arrested on 25.09.2025 and he has been in judicial custody since then.

5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
6.
The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is a 68 year old man and he is innocent of the allegations levelled against him.
7. The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the bail plea of the petitioner.

2 8.

It is relevant to extract the observation of the learned Sessions Judge in paragraph 7 of Annexure A2 order, which reads thus:-
"7.
The report as well as the case diary that has been produced reveal that there is a prima facie case against the petitioner.
The accused is alleged to have committed penetrative sexual assault on the girl on several occasions.
The nature of the alleged incident as revealed from the records and the absence of materials to suggest a false implication go a long way in revealing a prima facie case.
The report 2025:KER:94344 further reveals that there is a chance for involving of another children in the same nature of sexual assault.
The investigation is in progress only.
The security of the witnesses is another concern.
Also the fear element in the mind of the victim should be considered.
The case diary has been gone into and it shows that the girl child had been subjected to a physical examination of the victim.
There are enough materials to see that the medical examination of the victim also supports the prosecution version details being omitted.
7. On going through the Case Diary and the observations of the learned Sessions Judge, I am of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to be released on bail.
The bail application is dismissed as above.

Sd/-
